text: 17-year-old male. The patient presents with a 3-day history of pain in his left wrist, which worsened this morning accompanied by chills and malaise. speaker: Doctor
text: Did you notice any rash on your palms or soles, and do you recall seeing a bullseye rash or a tick bite during your trip to Minnesota? I will also examine your wrists and knees for signs of inflammation.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Pain in the left wrist. I also have Chills, Malaise, Painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on both wrists and hands, Swelling and erythema of the left wrist, Severe tenderness to palpation and passive movement of the left wrist.

speaker: Doctor
text: The painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands and wrists are highly specific for secondary syphilis, despite the Lyme-endemic travel history. REQUEST TEST: RPR, Treponemal antibody test, Lyme serology

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the negative syphilis and Lyme tests, let's consider other causes for your vesicular lesions and monoarthritis. Have you noticed any similar lesions on your trunk or face, or any recent exposure to animals or insects other than ticks?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Otherwise healthy with no significant past medical history. Social history: Admits to being sexually active with one female partner who uses a diaphragm for contraception. Recently went on a camping trip to Minnesota.

speaker: Doctor
text: The combination of monoarthritis, fever, and painless violaceous vesiculopustular lesions on the hands after camping in Minnesota is classic for disseminated gonococcal infection. REQUEST TEST: Gram stain and culture of synovial fluid, NAAT for Neisseria gonorrhoeae from urine and pharynx.
